title: V8 Hidden Classes (Shapes)
concept: The V8 engine uses an internal map called a 'Hidden Class' to speed up property access on objects.

steps.title: Creating p1: hidden class creation
steps.explanation:
When `new Point(1, 2)` runs, the V8 engine creates a `Hidden Class` to remember the 'shape' of this object.
Each time a property is added, the object transitions to a new hidden class.
1. A hidden class C0 is created for the empty object
2. `this.x = 1` causes a transition from C0 to C1 (x added)
3. `this.y = 2` causes a transition from C1 to C2 (y added)
`p1` ends up with hidden class C2.
steps.keyInsight: Adding a property isn't just 'storing a value' — it triggers an internal structure change (Transition).

steps.title: Creating p2: reusing the hidden class
steps.explanation:
When creating `p2`, V8 notices that the property addition order and structure are identical to `p1`.
So instead of creating a new hidden class, it reuses the C2 hidden class that `p1` already established.
This makes property access very fast.
steps.keyInsight: Initializing properties in the same order lets the engine treat objects as the 'same type' and optimize them.

steps.title: Adding a property: hidden class branch
steps.explanation:
After object creation, we dynamically add the `z` property to `p1` only.
Since the existing C2 hidden class has no information about `z`, V8 creates a new hidden class C3 (C2 + z) and transitions `p1` to C3.
Now `p1` and `p2` have different hidden classes, reducing optimization efficiency.
steps.keyInsight: Dynamically adding properties after object creation is the main culprit for breaking optimization.

steps.title: Printing p1 properties
steps.explanation:
Printing `p1`'s `x` and `z` properties.
`p1` uses the new hidden class C3 to locate the values.

steps.title: Printing p2 properties
steps.explanation:
Printing `p2`'s `x` property.
`p2` still uses the original hidden class C2.

quiz.question: What is the best practice for maintaining V8's Hidden Class optimization?
options: Initialize all properties in order inside the constructor
Add properties on the fly whenever needed (obj.newProp = 1)
Change the property initialization order each time (x, y → y, x)
Frequently delete properties with the delete operator
quiz.explanation: Defining properties in order inside the constructor ensures all created objects share the same hidden class, giving you the best performance.

misconceptions.wrong: JavaScript objects are HashMaps, so they're slow
misconceptions.correct: V8 uses hidden classes to access properties as fast as **array offsets**.
misconceptions.why: Early JS engines used hash maps, but modern V8 introduced hidden classes to achieve property access speeds comparable to statically typed languages like C++ and Java.

keyTakeaway: Keep your objects' 'shape' consistent. Consistency is speed.
